node.title: Re^3: Accessing 2 multidimensional arrays simultaneously
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [Ppeoc],

I see what you mean. If it's always the first row, it's fairly simple: print join(",", @{$a1[0]}, @{$a2[0]}), "\n"; - for an explanation of the dereferencing syntax see [doc://perlreftut] and maybe [doc://perldsc]. If you want to do this to all the rows, assuming both arrays have the same number of rows, just add a loop:

my @a1 = ( ['a','b','c'], ['d','e','f'], ['g','h','i'] ); my @a2 = ( ['j','k','l'], ['m','n','o','p'], ['q','r'] ); for my $r (0..$#a1) { print join(",", @{$a1[$r]}, @{$a2[$r]}), "\n"; } __END__ a,b,c,j,k,l d,e,f,m,n,o,p g,h,i,q,r

And if you want single quotes around the values: print join(",", map {"'$_'"} @{$a1[0]}, @{$a2[0]}), "\n";

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
